newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rebels overrun police post, killing 22.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rebels overrun police post, killing 22.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels on Saturday overran a remote police post in Sri Lanka's north, killing at least 22 policemen and wounding 18, a police official in northern Sri Lanka said.

About 200 rebels, armed with mortars and small arms, attacked the police post at Kebitigollewa, 220 km (135 miles) northeast of Colombo, just before daybreak on Saturday, said the police official, who asked not to be named.
At least five among the 18 wounded policemen were said to be in serious condition, the official said.
A Defence Ministry spokesman in Colombo told Reuters at least eight policemen, including civilian homeguards, were believed killed in the attack.
"Details of the attack are just coming in. A clearing operation (by the army) in the area is now going on," he said.
Several Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had been killed in the attack, the ministry spokesman said.
The rebels' official Voice of Tiger radio station did not mention the attack in its Saturday morning broadcast.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Saturday's attack followed intensified fighting between government troops and the rebels earlier in the week.
On Thursday, air force helicopter gunships destroyed a coastal Tamil rebel camp at Nachchikudah in the northwestern Mannar district, killing at least 10 rebels, according to the Defence Ministry.
The gunships destroyed a communication tower in the camp and sank two large rebel speedboats which were trying to flee the base, the ministry said.

But the Voice of Tigers radio said in a Saturday morning broadcast Thursday's helicopter attack had wounded at least five civilians, including two teenagers and a five-year old boy. It did not mention any casualties in the Tigers' ranks.
Civilians were forced to flee Nachchikudah to nearby villages for safety, the rebel radio said.
The air force says it only targets those rebel camps that are not in the vicinity of villages.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
